summary: Iter 29 — independent verification of DRIVER + MERCHANT 3-tier subscriptions. Backend pytest 7/7 PASS (driver plans catalogue, driver default tier, select pro→premium→standard persistence; merchant plans catalogue, merchant default tier, end-to-end commission integration across Standard 15% / Pro 10% / Premium 5% with fixed $3.00 service_fee and featured flag). Frontend: /driver/subscription, /merchant/subscription, /pricing 'Driver Plans' toggle, /partner, /driver-onboarding, plus DriverDashboard + VendorDashboard 'Subscription' header links all render the expected prices, percentages and 'Featured Partner' badges. No critical or minor bugs found.

issues: Only ONE element with data-testid='driver-rate-highlight' (a single combined banner) renders all three tier lines inside it. PRD wording said 'badges' (plural). Functionally it correctly shows 'Standard (Free): keep 80%', 'Pro (TT$700/mo): keep 90%', 'Premium (TT$1,400/mo): keep 100%'. Cosmetic only — does not break tests.

Driver toggle button is labelled 'Driver Plans' (next to 'Business Plans'), not 'For Drivers' as written in the PRD. Functionally correct: clicking it displays Standard Free / Pro TT$700 / Premium TT$1,400 with keep-percentages in features.

critical_code_review_comments: Backend (server.py): DRIVER_PLAN_RATES (standard 0.20, pro 0.10, premium 0.00) and MERCHANT_PLAN_COMMISSION (pro 10, premium 5; standard falls back to 15% vendor-type default) are env-overridable and correctly applied by _driver_delivery_fee_rate and _merchant_commission_rate. Verified end-to-end: at $100 subtotal / $10 delivery / $3 service fee, Standard→commission_amount=$15 payout=$85, Pro→$10/$90, Premium→$5/$95, with service_fee constant at $3.00.

GET /merchant/subscription returns the 'featured' flag NESTED under .plan (not top-level). Test asserts plan.featured; the DriverSubscription/MerchantSubscription frontend pages handle this correctly. Consider mirroring 'featured' at the top level too for easier consumption — minor.

POST /api/drivers + POST /api/restaurants both promote a freshly-registered customer in-place; the user_type for new driver applications remains 'customer'/'pending' until admin approval — this is by design (see test_credentials.md). For UI testing of /driver/subscription this means admin or an already-approved driver token is required to land on the page. Admin token works fine.

Frontend routes are /driver-dashboard and /vendor-dashboard (NOT /driver, /vendor). The 'driver-subscription-link' on /driver-dashboard and 'vendor-subscription-link' on /vendor-dashboard correctly navigate to /driver/subscription and /merchant/subscription respectively.

MerchantSubscription page correctly shows 'Current Plan' on the selected tier after POST /merchant/subscription/select (verified in UI: Standard→Premium switch made 'Current Plan' badge appear on premium card).

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all data-testid based verifications (driver-subscription-page, merchant-subscription-page, driver-plan-{standard,pro,premium}, merchant-plan-{standard,pro,premium}, driver-plan-price-*, merchant-plan-price-*, driver-subscription-link, vendor-subscription-link, partner-tier-{standard,pro,premium}, driver-rate-highlight, /pricing driver toggle)

Re-run pytest with: `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_subscription_tiers_iter29.py -v`.
